reviews.title: Loved it, would like to have spent longer there.
reviews.text: 5 of 5 bubblesLoved it, would like to have spent longer there.A really easy to find hotel that took me 20 minutes to walk to from the train station with wheeled hand luggage. The panoramic views as I walked towards the hotel were stunning with the mountainous backdrop. It is a quaint family run hotel in a quiet location but still, close to everything. Check in was simple, friendly & hassle free & I was advised of the WiFi password, breakfast times, check out time & instructions on how to enter the hotel if I returned to it late or in the early hours. With 1 lift & my room key (not a keycard & needed to enter the hotel at later hours) in hand, I was on the way up to my room in just a few short minutes after entering the hotel.My room was on the smallish side but fine as I was travelling solo. It was very clean with a laminate wood floor, 2 single beds pushed together, luggage rack, large mirror, wall mounted tv, safe, clothes rail, electric fan, chair, small shelf/workspace, smoke alarm & a number of electrical sockets. WiFi was password activated, quick to connect to, had fast speeds & was consistent & reliable. Two windows meant an abundance of natural light & I had no issues with noise from inside or outside of the hotel.The bathroom was not massive but was still an adequate size. Very clean with tiled floor & fully tiled walls, hairdryer, mirror, towels, a small shower cubicle with a shower head & hose on a rail, good water pressure & plenty of hot water, wall vent, 2 small bars of soap, 4 small bottles of hair/bodywash, shower hat & vanity kit.Breakfast, served from 07:00 – 10:00, was an excellent continental buffet with no need to book a time. Plenty to choose from with toasts, breads, pastries, cereals, cheeses, cold meat slices, yoghurt, bacon, scrambled eggs, boiled eggs, whole apples, grapes, figs, sliced cucumber, tomatoes, peppers, melon & pineapple, honey, Nutella & other spreads, teas, coffees, orange juice & iced tea.Directly across the road from the hotel is a café/restaurant/bar called Sandwirt that was recommended to me on checking in & it didn’t disappoint. Family owned & run it was chilled, very laid back, frequented by friendly & chatty locals, served up great food, really nice Tirolean beer called Starkenberger & the prices were very reasonable. The owners too, were very friendly & welcoming. If you fancy something a little (well actually a lot) livelier without straying too far from the hotel, further up the street heading towards the bridge for the old town is M&M cocktail bar. It was very busy & again, very popular with the locals but with a much younger clientele than at Sandwirt. I was the last customer to leave as I enjoyed a pleasant conversation with the very friendly bar staff. I’m not a fan of cocktails so I didn’t try any but I am a fan of beer & I had 3 very refreshing & tasty pints of Trumer Pils which cost 4.50 Euros each for 500 mls. If your fancy is Indian food, there are 3 Indian restaurants on the same street as the hotel, all located between the hotel & the bridge as you walk towards the old town. There is an atm located less than 200 mts from the hotel. If the purpose of your stay is to visit the old town & the Golden Roof, it is an easy stroll of just 10 minutes or a little bit under.Read more

reviews.title: Austrian experience
reviews.text: 4 of 5 bubblesAustrian experienceStayed 3 nights in Hotel Gasthof Engl. We emailed the owner 1 week before arrival, seeking advise for directions to the hotel but they didn’t reply. So we had to use Google map and make our way to the hotel on foot, which takes around 25mins from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof. For fellow travellers, who do not wish to walk so long, my advise is to take bus 501 (just in front of the train station) and stop at no 4 Innstraße- see the last photo I have posted. The bus comes around every 30mins from Monday to Friday. On weekends the timing may change. If you buy the Innsbruck card from the tourist centre, all bus and tram rides are included. This hotel is located across the river, takes around 10- 15mins walk to the old town. If you want to visit mountain Nordkette, there is a funicular station around 15 mins walk from the left side of the hotel. The hotel has a lift. So it’s good for traveller with heavy luggages. The room itself is reasonably sized, clean and has got electrical socket on each side of the bed to charge your devices. We stay in level 2 and was able to see the snow cap mountain view. There are however 2 things which I don’t like about this room. First is that the ventilation mainly comes from the window. As it’s along a street, it can be a bit noisy at night  if you open the window for ventilation. Second is about is bed and pillow- they are way too soft.  The hotel provide breakfast and I must say it’s quite good spread. There are yogurt, good selection of jams, hams, fruits and bread. If you bring a Thermo flask, they help to refill hot water as well since there are no kettle in the room. Overall this is a small family owned hotel, it is not fanciful but compensated by its location (close to old town) and hearty breakfast spread. Good for those who want a feel of Austrian guesthouse.Read more

reviews.title: Extremely Poor Customer Service
reviews.text: 1 of 5 bubblesExtremely Poor Customer ServiceI booked with Hotel Engl and had a terribly negative experience. I can overlook an honest mistake, but when the owner does not take responsibility for the mistake and blames the customer and makes excuses, it's unacceptable. I am reviewing this hotel based on my experience. I arrived from Amsterdam July 2, 2017 as reserved. It was early in the day and the room was understandably not ready. My daughter was not feeling well so I told the owner my daughter might want to stay in the room that day when it was ready. The owner said she would rush room cleaning, which I appreciated. We left the luggage and were told it would be put in our room and we could pick the key up later. Friends picked us up and took us to breakfast. My daughter began to feel better so we left to visit a museum a few hours away. Due to some problems and the weather, we realized we were not going to make it back to Innsbruck before the hotel desk closed at 10pm. I called the property around 8pm and spoke with the owner. I told her we would not be back to the hotel before 10pm and asked that she leave the key. She said that would be fine, told me the key would be in the lock box near the front door and gave me the code to the box. We arrived after 11:30pm and unlocked the lock box. There was no key in the lock box as the owner stated there would be. We rang the bell, tried the phone, walked around the building and spoke with a person who lived in the area. There was no way to get into the hotel. There was no emergency number. We were four women at midnight who could not get in the hotel and could not get an answer. Luckily, I was with a friend who lives in Innsbruck. We went to her house, without our luggage and our medicine and toiletries, and stayed until she took us back the next morning. When I spoke with the owner at the front desk the next morning, she asked if she could help me. I was wearing the same clothes as the day before. I explained that our key was not left as promised and we had to spend the night elsewhere. Her first words were, "That has never happened before." She finally apologized, but then said:She thought we were coming back earlier because my daughter felt bad.She has four children.She cannot afford to hire 24 hour help.Hotels in Europe don't have 24 hour help.The employee who was supposed to leave the key was very good, but she would speak to her.She would not charge me for that night. I asked if we could take breakfast to the room and she said no, because it was a buffet and that would be difficult. How difficult would it be to take a plate of food upstairs ourselves after 4 hours of sleep on the sofa of a friend? The owner was not accommodating at all. There is no reason for her excuses. What if my flight arrived after 10pm, as must happen frequently? Surely a hotel accommodates people with a way to get the key after closing time. I was treated like a bad college student returning late to a dorm, rather than a paying customer. Booking.com has a no-show status on my account. That is incorrect.  I booked it. I showed up. I checked in. I cancelled the remainder of my reservation and moved to a hotel with much better customer service.Read more

reviews.title: Fine stay in Innsbruck
reviews.text: 4 of 5 bubblesFine stay in InnsbruckStayed in the hotel for one night for business.  Hotel was easy enough to reach from the airport - take the bus until it goes across the river and then either walk the rest of the way there or wait for the W bus.  I had a very cozy room with an updated bathroom.  Both were clean.  You can see the care that the owners put into decorating the hotel.  It may not be uber trendy but everything is very functional and traditional.  Beds were very comfortable.  Breakfast was as good as any other hotel, with a good selection of foods.  I asked for the wifi password at the reception and got the code for two hours of free access.  It worked fine to upload backups of all the great photos of the mountains and other areas in Innsbruck.  The street outside tends to get a bit of traffic, but the room was not loud by any means.  Will be back for sure!Read more
